title: Make the drift and readiness signals stable, then release them
goal: Three signals the new checks emit are wrong in ways that would erode them. (1) The readiness check fails every agent worktree that is merely behind origin/main (9 commits after a few merges), but syncing is the loop's own first step on a clean tree, so that is a step to report, not a blocker. (2) Its 'behind' line prints a bare number with a stray newline because the git output is not stripped. (3) Release drift counts task-close commits, which move one file under .agents/tasks and add no code: after a release lands, the very next task close makes the installed release read as behind. Count only non-merge commits that touched files outside .agents/tasks, in both scripts/check-release-sync.sh and susi workflow check, then cut and promote the release that carries the fix so every signal is green and stays green.
